job posting.d: A public ad that describes an open job, its requirements and, often, its pay and benefits.
job posting.ex: I found the job posting on the company's careers page.

qualifications.d: The skills, experience or education you need for a job.
qualifications.ex: She has all the qualifications listed in the ad.

reverse chronological.d: Ordered from the most recent to the oldest.
reverse chronological.es: en orden cronológico inverso (de lo más reciente a lo más antiguo)
reverse chronological.ex: List your jobs in reverse chronological order.

action verb.d: A strong verb that shows what you did, like 'led', 'built' or 'reduced'.
action verb.ex: Start every bullet with an action verb.

applicant tracking systems.d: Software that companies use to collect, sort and search the resumes they receive.
applicant tracking systems.ex: Many applicant tracking systems search resumes for key words from the ad.

benefits package.d: Everything an employer offers besides salary, such as health insurance, paid time off and a retirement plan.
benefits package.ex: The benefits package includes dental insurance and a 401(k).

onboarding.d: The process of welcoming and preparing a new employee: paperwork, training and introductions.
onboarding.es: incorporación (proceso de bienvenida de un nuevo empleado)
onboarding.ex: Onboarding takes about two weeks at our company.

new hire.d: A person who has just joined a company.
new hire.ex: Every new hire meets with HR on the first day.

article.dek: How recruiters read resumes and job ads, what a U.S.-style resume leaves out, and what happens after you get the offer.
article.title: Seven Seconds to Make It Count: Resumes, Job Ads and Your First Days in a U.S. Job

blocks.en: In the United States, hiring usually follows the same path: a company publishes a [[job posting]], collects resumes, screens them, interviews a short list of candidates, makes an offer and welcomes the new person. The first filter is fast. In a 2018 eye-tracking study by the job site Ladders, recruiters spent about 7.4 seconds on their first look at a resume. Resumes with a simple layout, clear headings and short bullet points did best; crowded pages with long sentences did worst.{1}
blocks.es: En Estados Unidos, la contratación casi siempre sigue el mismo camino: una empresa publica una vacante, recibe currículums, los filtra, entrevista a una lista corta de candidatos, hace una oferta y da la bienvenida a la nueva persona. El primer filtro es rápido. En un estudio de seguimiento ocular de 2018 del sitio de empleo Ladders, los reclutadores dedicaron unos 7.4 segundos a la primera mirada de un currículum. Los currículums con un diseño sencillo, encabezados claros y viñetas cortas funcionaron mejor; las páginas saturadas y con oraciones largas, peor.

blocks.h: A U.S. resume is not a Latin American CV
blocks.en: Career advisers at Harvard recommend listing your experience in [[reverse chronological]] order, starting each line with an [[action verb]], adding numbers when you can, and avoiding personal pronouns like “I.” They also say to leave out a photo, your age and your gender.{2} This is not only a question of style. The EEOC, the federal agency that enforces U.S. anti-discrimination laws, advises employers not to ask for an applicant's photograph, and warns that a job ad should not discourage people because of traits such as age or sex.{3}
blocks.es: Los asesores de carrera de Harvard recomiendan poner tu experiencia en orden cronológico inverso, empezar cada línea con un verbo de acción, agregar números cuando puedas y evitar pronombres personales como “I”. También aconsejan no incluir foto, edad ni género. No es solo una cuestión de estilo. La EEOC, la agencia federal que aplica las leyes contra la discriminación en EE. UU., recomienda a los empleadores no pedir la fotografía de un candidato y advierte que un anuncio de empleo no debe desanimar a nadie por rasgos como la edad o el sexo.

blocks.en: In much of Latin America, it is common for a CV to include a photo, a date of birth, marital status and a long list of duties. In a U.S. office, that extra information can make your resume look out of place, and a list of duties only tells the reader what you were supposed to do, not what you achieved. The good news: your experience is already valuable. You just need to present it the way U.S. recruiters expect to read it.
blocks.es: En gran parte de América Latina es común que un CV incluya foto, fecha de nacimiento, estado civil y una larga lista de funciones. En una oficina de EE. UU., esa información extra puede hacer que tu currículum se vea fuera de lugar, y una lista de funciones solo le dice al lector lo que te tocaba hacer, no lo que lograste. La buena noticia: tu experiencia ya es valiosa. Solo necesitas presentarla como los reclutadores de EE. UU. esperan leerla.

blocks.q_en: Look at your current CV. Does it include a photo, your age or your marital status? Does each job show a result, or only a list of duties?
blocks.q_es: Mira tu CV actual. ¿Incluye foto, tu edad o tu estado civil? ¿Cada trabajo muestra un resultado o solo una lista de funciones?

blocks.h: Three habits of strong job seekers

items.h: 1 · Read the job ad like a checklist
items.en: A job ad tells you exactly what the employer wants: the responsibilities, the required [[qualifications]] and often the pay and benefits. Many employers use [[applicant tracking systems]] to sort resumes, so Harvard's advisers suggest writing for both human readers and these systems.{2} Use the same key words as the ad when they truly describe your experience.
items.es: Un anuncio de empleo te dice exactamente qué quiere el empleador: las responsabilidades, los requisitos y muchas veces el sueldo y las prestaciones. Muchos empleadores usan sistemas de seguimiento de candidatos (ATS) para ordenar los currículums, por eso los asesores de Harvard sugieren escribir tanto para lectores humanos como para estos sistemas. Usa las mismas palabras clave del anuncio cuando de verdad describan tu experiencia.

items.en: Each bullet answers three questions: what did you do, how did you do it, and what was the result? Compare “Responsible for customer calls” with “Resolved 40+ customer calls a day in English and Spanish.” The second line shows impact, and a recruiter can see it in seconds.
items.es: Cada viñeta responde tres preguntas: qué hiciste, cómo lo hiciste y cuál fue el resultado. Compara “Responsible for customer calls” con “Resolved 40+ customer calls a day in English and Spanish”. La segunda línea muestra impacto, y un reclutador lo ve en segundos.

items.h: 3 · Understand the whole offer and your first days
items.en: A U.S. job offer is more than a salary. Health insurance, paid leave and retirement plans are part of the [[benefits package]]: in June 2025, benefits were 29.8% of what private employers spent on compensation.{4} Then [[onboarding]] begins. Every [[new hire]] completes Form I-9, which verifies identity and authorization to work.{5} Ask questions: Gallup found that only 12% of employees strongly agree that their organization does a great job onboarding new employees.{6}
items.es: Una oferta de trabajo en EE. UU. es más que un sueldo. El seguro médico, los días pagados y los planes de retiro forman parte del paquete de prestaciones: en junio de 2025, las prestaciones fueron el 29.8 % de lo que los empleadores privados gastaron en compensación. Después empieza la incorporación (onboarding). Toda persona de nuevo ingreso llena el Formulario I-9, que verifica su identidad y su autorización para trabajar. Haz preguntas: Gallup encontró que solo el 12 % de los empleados está totalmente de acuerdo en que su organización hace un gran trabajo al incorporar a los nuevos empleados.

blocks.en: You don't need a perfect career to write a strong resume. You need a clear format, real achievements and the confidence to talk about them. In the three cases below, you will fix a resume, read a job ad the way a recruiter does, and handle your first day with HR.
blocks.es: No necesitas una carrera perfecta para escribir un currículum fuerte. Necesitas un formato claro, logros reales y la seguridad para hablar de ellos. En los tres casos que siguen vas a corregir un currículum, leer un anuncio de empleo como lo hace un reclutador y manejar tu primer día con Recursos Humanos.

cases.title_en: The Resume That Says Too Much
cases.scene: Luis, an accountant from Guadalajara, applies for a job in Phoenix. This is the experience section of his resume:

message.text: Accountant, Grupo Delta (2018–2024). I was in charge of doing the monthly reports and paying the suppliers. I am a responsible and hardworking person. Age: 36. Married, 2 children.

cases.outcome: The recruiter looks at it for a few seconds and moves on to the next resume.

activity.model:
Accountant | Grupo Delta | Guadalajara, MX | 2018–2024
• Prepared monthly financial reports for 3 business units, always on deadline
• Processed payments to 120+ suppliers and reduced late fees by 30%
• Created an Excel checklist that cut month-end closing errors

Add a number or a result

cases.scene: Ana finds this job ad and wants to decide if she should apply:

message.text: Bilingual HR Assistant – Full-time, Dallas, TX. Requirements: 2+ years of HR or administrative experience; fluent English and Spanish. You will: schedule interviews, prepare onboarding paperwork and answer employee questions about benefits. We offer: medical and dental insurance, a 401(k) with company match, and paid time off.

cases.outcome: Ana uses the same key words in her resume and gets a call for a phone interview.

parts.t: Bilingual HR Assistant – Full-time, Dallas, TX.
Requirements: 2+ years of HR or administrative experience; fluent English and Spanish.

why.en: The required qualifications: check that you meet them and show them clearly on your resume.
why.es: Los requisitos: revisa que los cumples y muéstralos con claridad en tu currículum.

parts.t: You will: schedule interviews, prepare onboarding paperwork and answer employee questions about benefits.

why.en: The responsibilities: these are the key words to use in your bullets, if they describe what you've done.
why.es: Las responsabilidades: son las palabras clave para tus viñetas, si describen lo que has hecho.

parts.t: We offer: medical and dental insurance, a 401(k) with company match, and paid time off.

why.en: The benefits package: part of the offer. Compare it, not only the salary.
why.es: El paquete de prestaciones: es parte de la oferta. Compáralo, no solo el sueldo.

activity.prompt_es: Toca las tres partes del anuncio que Ana debe leer con más atención.

cases.title_es: Tu primer día con Recursos Humanos
cases.scene: On his first day, Carlos receives his onboarding packet: Form I-9, the benefits enrollment forms and the employee handbook. The HR manager asks: “Any questions?”

options.text: No, it's fine. I'll look at it later.
Yes, thank you. Could you walk me through the [[benefits package]]? I'd like to choose my health plan before the enrollment deadline.

activity.prompt_en: Tap the answer you would choose.

why.en: Answer B is more professional: Carlos asks a clear question, shows that he takes ownership of his paperwork, and avoids missing an important deadline. Answer A sounds polite, but he may lose time or benefits later.
why.es: La respuesta B es más profesional: Carlos hace una pregunta clara, muestra que se hace responsable de sus trámites y evita perder una fecha importante. La respuesta A suena amable, pero después podría perder tiempo o prestaciones.

questions: Which answer would you choose? Why?
What would you ask HR on your first day in a U.S. company?
questions_es: ¿Qué le preguntarías a Recursos Humanos en tu primer día en una empresa de EE. UU.?
